Approval is effectively assured by voting and support agreements. Next: DOJ Second Request compliance, then a clearance, consent-decree or suit decision. Close guided to 1H27.
verified.instrument: Long ROKU and short 0.9693 FOXA per share to hedge the stock leg. A naked long ROKU leaves you holding FOXA price risk as well as deal risk.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 yes: named acquirer (Fox Corp). G2 yes: signed merger agreement with a fixed $96 cash + 0.9693 FOXA exchange ratio. G3 weak: the specific figure is the ~$3.64 (2.4%) gross spread, and the market already prices it as compensation for DOJ risk, so it is not unpriced.
verified.edge: L. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: about +26%. The base is ~$121, backed out from the 33.7% premium to the close before the sale-process reports; ROKU is $152.85 today. Remaining: about +2.4% gross to the $156.49 implied value (96 + 0.9693 x FOXA $62.41, FMP 2026-10-12), over roughly 6-9 months to a 1H27 close. That is about 3-5% annualized, near or below cash yields. The deal breaks if DOJ sues over self-preferencing of Fox content on Roku's home screen, and the break downside to ~$120-125 is about -20%, which dwarfs the spread. The spread has also narrowed as the offer value fell from $162 to $156 with FOXA. Mostly harvested, so the score is capped.
verified.primary_source: Fox Corp FY2026 10-K (sec.gov, filed Aug 2026): $96 cash + 0.9693 FOXA, signed 2026-06-14. Fox S-4/424B3 (2026): $162.20 implied at the 2026-06-11 unaffected close. Semafor 2026-09-08 plus Fox SEC filing 2026-09-09: DOJ Second Request. FMP quotes 2026-10-12: ROKU $152.85, FOXA $62.41.
verified.analysis: The deal is real, specific and still ahead. The 10-K confirms the signed agreement and fixed ratio, and the DOJ Second Request was reported 2026-09-08 and confirmed in an SEC filing the next day. The shareholder vote is a formality because voting agreements are in place. But about 90% of the move from the undisturbed price is already captured. The remaining ~2.4% gross spread is thin pay for a live vertical-antitrust Second Request and a 6-9 month hold. Upside is about $3.6 per share against roughly $30 per share on a break, so the risk/reward is poor. The cash and fixed-ratio terms are contractual, so the provenance check does not apply. Gap: I did not confirm the Oct 14 meeting date in the definitive proxy.

verified.catalyst: C.H. Robinson (CHRW) is acquiring 100% of RXO for $17.25 cash plus 0.0856 CHRW shares per share. Holders can elect all-cash $30.25 or all-stock 0.1992, prorated to about 57% cash / 43% stock. The deal was announced 2026-10-05 and is expected to close in 1H27, subject to regulatory approval and an RXO shareholder vote.
verified.dated_milestone: Announced 2026-10-05. Next steps are the HSR filing and waiting period, the S-4/proxy, and the RXO shareholder vote, likely around 1Q27; no date has been set. Expected close is 1H27.
verified.instrument: RXO common, long. A classic arb would short 0.0856 CHRW per RXO share to hedge the stock leg.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 passes: named counterparty, CHRW. G2 passes: signed merger agreement, unanimous board approvals, $4.5B committed financing plus a Morgan Stanley bridge, and a voting agreement from MFN Partners (about 17% of shares). G3 fails: no specific unpriced figure remains, because the spread is about 1.2%.
verified.edge: L. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base is +24%. The Oct-2 close was about $23.45 (implied by the 29% premium to $30.25); RXO now trades at $29.08. Remaining capture is about +1.2%. Live consideration is $17.25 + 0.0856 x $142.31 (CHRW) = $29.43, a gross spread of $0.35, or roughly 2% annualized over 6-9 months, which is below the risk-free rate. If the deal breaks, downside is about -19% back to around $23.5, so upside/downside is about 0.06. The fixed exchange ratio means CHRW weakness also eats the spread: CHRW is down from a $151.88 VWAP to $142.31, so the headline $30.25 is now $29.43. The event is real but almost fully harvested.
verified.primary_source: RXO Form 425 filings on SEC EDGAR (merger announcement, 2026-10-05): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001929561/000119312526413211/d115124d425.htm. FreightWaves deal report, 2026-10-05. FMP batch-quote, 2026-10-12: RXO $29.08, CHRW $142.31.
verified.analysis: The deal is real, specific and dated: a signed agreement, committed financing and a 17% holder locked up. Price provenance is contractual, so it is exempt from the waterfall check. But the market has already priced most of it. RXO is at $29.08 against live consideration of $29.43, leaving about 1.2% gross (around 2% annualized) after a +24% run-up. Against that sits roughly 19% break downside, plus antitrust review of a merger of two large truckload brokers and exposure to CHRW price swings. Mostly harvested with negative risk-adjusted carry, so tier NONE. Gap: I did not check the HSR timing or second-request status, or any regulator commentary.

verified.catalyst: RYAM's board-run strategic review, with Morgan Stanley and Wachtell advising and a possible sale of the whole company on the table, is guided to conclude with a "clear path forward" in Q4-2026. A named bidder sits behind it: AIP's documented, rejected $11-12/share cash proposal against a $7.02 stock.
verified.dated_milestone: Review conclusion guided for Q4-2026 (by 2026-12-31). Next date: the Q3-2026 earnings release, expected in early November. The triage says Nov-5; last year's pattern was a Nov-4 release with the call the next day, and the 2026 date is not yet confirmed.
verified.bloom_gates: G1: named counterparty, American Industrial Partners (AIP Capital Fund VIII), in a Schedule 13D exhibit letter dated 2025-11-18. G3: a specific unpriced figure, $11.00-12.00/share all-cash, with no financing condition and a go-shop, 99-117% above the 2025-11-17 close. G2 is only partial: management guides the review to conclude in Q4-2026 but has not committed to any transaction, and says there is no assurance of one.
verified.edge: M. Run-up: the pre-catalyst base is about $5.53 (implied by the bid's 99-117% premium to the 2025-11-17 close). Today's $7.02 is +27% above that. Remaining capture: +64% from $7.02 to the $11.50 midpoint, or +57% to the $11 floor. So most of the upside is still on the table. The market implies roughly 25% odds of a deal (($7.02-$5.5)/($11.5-$5.5)). The stock has slid from about $9 in July to $7, below both its 50-day ($8.35) and 200-day ($8.66) averages. This is a binary, unharvested setup, but the bid is stale and was rejected. The edge is medium, not high: the tape is fading the deal, and a "path forward" could just as easily mean a standalone plan or partial asset sales.
verified.primary_source: AIP Schedule 13D exhibit (proposal letter dated 2025-11-18, SEC accession 0000950103-26-002612). RYAM Q2-2026 8-K and earnings release (2026-08-04). RYAM 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-27. Review launch: Jax Daily Record (2026-04-20). CEO appointment: Jax Daily Record (2026-06-25). FMP quote, 2026-10-12: $7.02.
verified.kill_fact: Correction, and it helps the line: the claim "no evidence AIP is in the current process" is wrong. AIP's 13D/A, filed 2026-07-15 with an event date of 2026-07-14, says AIP signed the Issuer's standard confidentiality agreement, with a standstill, in connection with the formal strategic-alternatives process announced 2026-04-20. AIP holds 3.4M shares (5.04%, about $25.4M cost, roughly $7.48 average). The filing says AIP may submit non-binding proposals, but it makes no new price commitment. The Q2-2026 8-K (EX-99.1, 2026-08-04) confirms the company expects "to conclude the review and communicate a clear path forward during the fourth quarter", and the CEO cites several "interested parties". The deal has not fired and is not priced in. The stock is $7.02 against a 50-day average of $8.35 and a 52-week high of $11.85, so it is fading into the decision with about 57-71% to run to the $11-12 bid. The real risks: (1) a "clear path forward" can be a partial asset sale or a stand-alone plan, and secured lenders (net secured leverage about 4.3x) would take those proceeds before the common does; (2) the $11-12 figure is a rejected, non-binding letter from 2025-11-18, not a live price; (3) if no sale comes, the levered equity could retest about $5.4. No 8-K or deal news was found from September to 2026-10-12.
verified.analysis: The triage's "unconfirmed" $11-12 bid is now CONFIRMED in AIP's Schedule 13D exhibit letter. That letter was dated 2025-11-18, the board rejected the bid in December 2025, and AIP disclosed it in February 2026. The Q2-2026 release (2026-08-04) and the 10-Q both guide the review to conclude in Q4-2026. Capital-structure check (10-Q, quarter ended 2026-06-27): about $812M debt principal (term loan of about $691M due 2029) against $57M cash, so net debt is about $755M against a $473M market cap. Nothing senior sits ahead of the common except a $12.2M BioNova subsidiary preferred. That means a cash deal price flows straight to the common, and the $11-12 is contractual-style, not derived. The equity is highly levered, though, and RYAM lost $420M in 2025, so a no-deal outcome likely retests the $5.4 low. Risks: there is no evidence AIP is in the current process. In June the board named a permanent CEO, Daniel Krawczyk (an M&A operator), and RBC read that as making a sale somewhat less likely. No news from September or October was found. Gaps: I did not verify change-of-control or debt-portability terms, any bidder other than AIP, or the confirmed Q3 date.
